questions.title: Planning an experiment — ball & compressed spring

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Diagram: a spring with one end against a block clamped to the bench (G-clamp); a steel ball of radius r held against the spring, compressing it by a distance x; a light gate at a fixed point P (connected to a timer) to measure the speed of the ball.
Procedure and measurements: vary the radius r (independent variable) and measure the speed v of the ball at P (dependent variable), keeping the compression x constant. Determine r by measuring the diameter d with calipers/a micrometer (r = d/2), repeating in different directions and averaging. Determine v = diameter of ball/time recorded by the light gate at P. Measure x with a rule (x = original length − compressed length).
Analysis: plot a graph of lg(v²) (or 2 lg v) against lg r. The relationship is valid if a straight line is produced (with a non-zero y-intercept). From v² = Ykx²/(rⁿρ): gradient = −n, so n = −gradient; y-intercept = lg(Ykx²/ρ), so Y = 10^(y-intercept) × ρ/(kx²).
Controls: keep k, ρ and x constant. Determine k by hanging a known mass and using k = mg/extension (or a force–extension graph, k = gradient). Determine ρ from the mass (balance) and volume: ρ = 3m/(4πr³). Keep x constant with a pin/rule/card marking the starting position. Adjust the light gate so the diameter of each ball cuts the beam.
Safety: prevent the ball leaving the bench (screens/cushions). Repeat each measurement for the same r and average v.

questions.title: Analysis of data — Hubble’s law & galaxy redshift

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
(λ − λ₀)/λ₀ = Hd/c, so λ = λ₀ + (Hλ₀)(d/c).
gradient = Hλ₀ and y-intercept = λ₀

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: Plot the six points of λ against d/c (within half a small square), each with a horizontal error bar on d/c.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: Draw a straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable line (steepest/shallowest line through all the error bars).

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: gradient ≈ 1.8 nm per 10¹⁵ s (from Δy/Δx over more than half the line's length). Absolute uncertainty = gradient of best fit − gradient of worst acceptable line.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.answer: y-intercept ≈ 658 nm (substituting a point into y = mx + c). Uncertainty = difference between the two intercepts.

parts.label: (e)
parts.answer:
T = 1/H = 1/(2.8 × 10⁻¹⁸) = 3.6 × 10¹⁷ s.
Absolute uncertainty found from the worst acceptable line (using Δλ₀ and Δgradient).
